key_insight: NeuronSoup evolves asynchronous temporal graph networks where shared hidden neurons accumulate state across paths, enabling interference-based computation without backpropagation.
engineering_relevance: The approach suggests a compact, non-differentiable alternative for adaptive computation in tasks where variable depth, timing, and pathway interactions matter.
method: Frozen ResNet18 features are fed into a network of variable-length paths with delay-mediated signal propagation.
Hidden neurons are shared across multiple paths, so later arrivals interact with residual state left by earlier ones.
A genetic algorithm co-evolves topology, weights, delays, and connectivity from a flat real-valued genome.
evidence_signal: On MNIST digit classification, the evolved model reached 85.9% test accuracy with 204 active paths, 266 hidden neurons, and a 115 KB model after 10,000 generations.
watch_item: The method is computationally expensive to evolve and its performance may depend heavily on the frozen encoder, task structure, and careful timing/delay implementation.
paper_title: NeuronSoup: Evolving Asynchronous, Shared-Neuron Temporal Graphs without Backpropagation
